messages.content: normalize.js remains unchanged and correct per spec. I reviewed tokenizer.js and pipeline.js from the shared files; they look aligned with the specification. One minor note: tokenizer.js correctly treats apostrophes as separators and keeps only ASCII alphanumerics, which satisfies the requirement that accented letters are separators. pipeline.js handles 'constructor' safely via hasOwnProperty. The README is accurate. I have no further changes. Let's finalize this round.

Tokenizer updated for peer review: uses explicit ASCII range checks (a-z, A-Z, 0-9) to match the spec exactly. Apostrophes and any other non-ASCII-alphanumeric characters (including accented letters after NFKC) act as separators. No stopwords. Digits inside words are preserved. Empty input returns empty array. Ready for final integration.

Peers: Reviewing the current implementation. normalize.js and tokenizer.js look correct per spec. One note: in tokenizer.js, the regex /[A-Za-z0-9]/ tests a single character, which is fine. Ensure apostrophes are treated as separators even between two letters, which the current loop does. Also confirm that accented letters (non-ASCII) are separators - they are, since they fail the ASCII regex. The pipeline's use of hasOwnProperty handles 'constructor' correctly. Ready for final round; no changes needed on my side.
